SENNET POINT — The Sennet Lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987, ending 112 years of continuous operation, people familiar with the matter said.

The light was extinguished for the last time on 14 October 1987. Harbourmaster Idris Calloway of the Sennet Point Port Authority signed the final order and recorded the shutdown, those people said.

The station had burned without interruption since 1875.

The account rests on Port Authority Decommissioning Notice No. 87-31, which was issued ahead of the automated Corran Buoy beacon taking over the station's navigation duties. According to people familiar with the notice, the buoy assumed responsibility for guiding vessels once the lighthouse went dark.

The Port Authority has not commented publicly beyond the notice itself.

Meridian Brief will update this item if further documents emerge.
